items.title: Serve Robotics launches new business to become the AWS for robots | TechCrunch
items.summary:
Serve Robotics, a maker of self-driving sidewalk delivery robots, is expanding beyond its autonomous delivery operations in a bid to become a technology supplier to other companies building robots.

The company, which spun out of Uber’s acquisition of Postmates in 2021 and went public in 2024, said Thursday it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services. [...] Specifically, Serve Robotics will offer customers its connectivity and data tools. Bedrock Robotics, a startup developing self-driving systems for construction equipment, is a customer, according to Serve. It’s also working with T-Mobile to bring AI computing power closer to robots, Serve announced alongside its third-quarter earnings on Thursday.

“We are solving the problem of robots in human spaces,” Serve Robotics CEO and co-founder Ai Kashani told TechCrunch. [...] Serve Robotics already makes two kinds of robots, the cute googly-eyed sidewalk delivery robot and one designed for hospitals that it got through its acquisition of Diligent Robotics.

Those businesses are not going away, Kashani emphasized in a recent interview. Instead, he said there is opportunity to sell the technology it developed for its own robots to other companies developing robots for farms, warehouses, and other uncontrolled environments.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: SHE NEEDS A FAN TO STAY COOL. THAT'S THE MOST REALISTIC PART OF THIS VIDEO. 🤖🌀
items.summary:
SHE NEEDS A FAN TO STAY COOL. THAT'S THE MOST REALISTIC PART OF THIS VIDEO. 🤖🌀

a robot expo. a crowd of phones. 
a girl with a glowing metal core where her waist should be. ✨
someone holds a little fan to it. she smiles, fixes her hair. 

the face? almost certainly AI. 
the fan? that's real robotics. 🔥
every motor, every battery, every AI chip makes heat. 🌡️
heat is one of the reasons real humanoids still work in short shifts and spend hours on chargers. 

so how far have robots actually come? 👇

📅 2015: at the DARPA challenge, robots fell over opening doors.
🤸 2025: humanoids do flips, box, and dance at expos.
📦 2025: Unitree shipped 5,500+ humanoids. AgiBot's CEO said 5,000+.
🇺🇸 Tesla, Figure and Agility: about 150 each (Omdia).
🏭 Hyundai plans a factory for 30,000 robots a year by 2028.

💰 Morgan Stanley: a $5 trillion humanoid market by 2050.
ten years from falling over to doing backflips. 
but the robots that exist are still grey, bulky and plugged in. 🔌

the "robot girl" is what the hype looks like.
the fan is what the engineering looks like. 🛠️
when the real ones catch up with this video, will you be able to tell the difference? 👀

items.title: 5/6 Eksperimen Simulasi
items.summary:
5/6 Eksperimen Simulasi  

Kami memvalidasi kriteria tersebut dalam dua pengaturan simulasi dengan protokol yang sama, dirata-ratakan dari tiga seed.  

Single-simulator (RoboMimic). Sumber dan target berbagi satu simulator, yang mengisolasi kriteria kurasi dari kesenjangan domain apa pun. Pada Lift, Square, dan Transport, TUCO adalah yang terbaik atau seri-terbaik dalam 18 dari 25 pengaturan tugas-anggaran, dan menyamai pelatihan all-data pada Lift hanya dengan menggunakan 25% dari data.  

Sim-to-sim (IsaacSim ke MuJoCo). Demo dihasilkan dalam satu simulator dan dievaluasi dalam simulator lain, sebuah pengganti terkendali untuk kesenjangan sim-to-real. TUCO adalah yang terbaik dalam 15 dari 18 pengaturan dan di atas seleksi acak dalam semua 18. Pool IsaacSim lengkap bahkan merugikan CupCake, sementara subset yang dikurasi memberikan hasil terbaik pada setiap tugas.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: FDA seeks input on telesurgery, autonomous robotics
items.summary: Rapid advances in artificial intelligence, machine learning and connectivity are driving expansion of robotic applications in a wide range of clinical settings, the FDA said. Increases in processing power, data storage and computational efficiency are enabling progress in robotic systems with autonomous capabilities. [...] In another example of teleoperation, manufacturers are developing devices that enable technicians to remotely perform ultrasounds, the FDA said. Robotic devices include stereotactic navigation systems, imaging devices and endoluminal navigation devices. [...] The FDA is asking the robotics community to submit comments on the discussion paper by Jan. 5. Ahead of that deadline, a public workshop to discuss the topics raised in the paper is scheduled for Dec. 2-3.
